Not recommended.

The game is way too short, and most of the time you’re just running around. A lot of the boss encounters across different chapters feel almost identical: sneak, hide, run, repeat. There are even some weird 2D-style sections that feel completely out of place.

The sense of direction is also terrible. Half the time I wasn’t confused by the puzzle itself — I just had no idea where the game wanted me to go.

The jumping and grabbing mechanics are especially exhausting to watch and play. The character constantly struggles to jump, grab onto things, climb up, or just misses and falls. It feels unnecessarily sluggish and frustrating.

Overall, the game feels less scary or tense and more tiring. It’s short, repetitive, and just not very fun.

Eu gosto de fazer comparações entre jogos porque, geralmente, existem outros games semelhantes por aí que ajudam a ilustrar a ideia básica de gameplay de determinados títulos. Nesse caso, pelo que ouvi dizer, Hades seria o game mais popular com similaridades com Sworn.

Nunca joguei Hades, então não sei dizer exatamente onde os sistemas dos dois divergem. Mas sei que esse jogo é muito bom e que existe a opção de jogá-lo em co-op com até 4 players.

A ideia é simples: você vai avançando entre salas, coletando power-ups típicos de roguelikes e aprimorando seu personagem. São 4 classes para escolher, e cada classe possui 4 opções diferentes de armas, que mudam completamente a forma como o combate funciona.

Considerando que o loop de gameplay é um tanto quanto simples, eu não recomendaria comprar o jogo pelo valor cheio. Mas, em uma boa promoção, esse jogo vale MUITO a pena!

A més a més, està ple de referències a altres videojocs coneguts com Skyrim i similars, i els secrets estan molt ben aconseguits. En concret m'encanta el de l'homenatge al grup de música Coure.

Caòtic, frenètic, visceral i addictiu, amb escenaris molt inmersius. Un gran representant dins del gènere, 10/10. I a més a més gratuït, res més a dir. Bona feina Roger!

I'm recommending this game for the gameplay, visuals, puzzles, and voice acting. Those people deserve praise and your money. Unfortunately the writing is so bad that it interferes with enjoying the game. This is especially obvious in the character Gina. During the entire Vatican level, Indy is solving puzzles solo. Once Gina joins him, he's incapable of solving anything without her. It's to the extent that whenever she is tagging along, you have to wait for her to point out a switch before you can interact with it.

They also messed up Gina's model just enough to hit uncanny valley. Everyone's eyes and expression matches the scene except hers. She ends up looking like a bug-eyed idiot blankly staring at nothing with her mouth agape. The actress is beautiful and does a good job with her lines so I can't help but wonder what went wrong.

White Shadows is a disturbingly beautiful and dark cinematic adventure inspired by Orwell's and other dystopias.

The comparison to classics like Limbo, Inside and Little Nightmares is easy, both in terms of gameplay and mood, but this game brings a truly unique take on the genre. Features a sinister carnival and a very oppressive society, and comes with a very accurate warning about racism, animal violence, and other sensitive themes.

Positive

•  Great ambiance with polished noir aesthetics
•  Smooth controls of creature at different stages
•  Impressive camera work frames different perspectives around 2D movement
•  Suitable classical soundtrack + distorted gibberish vocals
•  Disturbingly beautiful and dark with moody lighting
•  Classic puzzle mechanics (crates, machinery, levers, some timing)

Negative

•  Expected bigger ending twist or climax

A tiny, silly point and click that's way more replayable than you'd expect.

The more you play around with it, the more ways you find to untangle the little stories inside it. Love the art and visual style, is charming. It's a simple point and click at its core, but a really enjoyable one. You can mess around and see how many different ways you can solve a task or recruit companions along the way.

Great pick if you like short, quirky adventures with a lot of room to mess around and experiment.
